_comment: The one table that pins how a rejection fraction is spelled, driven by BOTH
rejectionNote.ts, the one-click 'Process target' result note) and
about the same run). The sentence around the number is word-identical on the
two screens — 'Cleaned ~N% of pixels — passing satellites, planes and
cosmic-ray hits were rejected' — so a divergence reads as the app quoting two
different numbers for one picture. Change the rule and you must change this
table, on both sides at once: frontend/src/components/target/
Cases are [fraction, expected]. It caught a live divergence the day it was
written: below 1% the frontend printed two decimals ('0.50%') where the
engine printed one ('0.5%'), and at the bottom of the cue's own band it
printed '0.07%' where the engine printed '<0.1%'. The frontend moved to the
engine's rule. The .x5 rows are the other half of the class: Python's round()
is half-to-even and JavaScript's Math.round is half-up.
